Magnetic order OurBigBook.com
Correlations that extend over a finite local distance without establishing macroscopic long-range order.

Magnetic sublattice

Words: 177
Magnetic order OurBigBook.com
A magnetic sublattice groups sites with a common ordered magnetic moment in a description of magnetic order. In the simplest two-sublattice description, assign magnetizations MA​ and MB​ per total specimen volume, so that
M=MA​+MB​,L=MA​−MB​.
(116)
Here L is one normalization of the staggered magnetization; conventions may include a factor 1/2. Using the same total volume for both contributions is essential. Equal magnetic moment per site does not imply equal sublattice contributions if the site populations differ.
In this six-site example, three A sites and three B sites give total magnetic moments 6m0​, 0, and 3m0​, respectively, along the chosen axis. The antiferromagnetic case has M=0 but L=6m0​z/V. Cancellation of the sum leaves the alternating information intact.

Magnetic neutron diffraction

Words: 740 Articles: 2
Magnetic order OurBigBook.com
Magnetic neutron diffraction uses scattering of neutrons by ordered magnetic moments to infer magnetic order. Neutrons also scatter from atomic nuclei, so a pattern can contain nuclear and magnetic contributions. A Bragg scattering peak encodes periodicity; it is not a photograph of an individual spin.
A minimal original calculation makes the extra periodicity visible. Consider identical nuclear scatterers at positions xn​=na, with equal neighboring separation a, and ordered magnetic moments alternating between +mA​ and −mB​. A two-site repeating block of length 2a has nuclear and magnetic scattering amplitudes, apart from common geometric factors,
FN​(q)=b(1+eiqa),FM​(q)=mA​−mB​eiqa,q=aπh​,h∈Z.
(117)
Here b is the common nuclear scattering coefficient and q the component of the scattering wave vector along the row. The magnetic expression assumes equally scattering point magnetic moments perpendicular to the scattering wave vector; real magnetic scattering measures the perpendicular component and has a momentum-dependent amplitude. This one-dimensional calculation is a periodicity illustration, not a finite-temperature solution for a chain.
For even h, FN​=2b and FM​=mA​−mB​. For odd h, FN​=0 and FM​=mA​+mB​. Thus equivalent opposing magnetic sublattices, mA​=mB​, cancel in forward scattering but reinforce at the odd positions of the doubled period. The intensity is proportional to the squared magnitude of the scattering amplitude, so changing an amplitude's sign does not make a negative intensity.
This calculation also exposes a useful difference between antiferromagnetism and ferrimagnetism: with mA​=2 and mB​=1, magnetic squared amplitudes are 1 at even h and 9 at odd h. Extra magnetic peaks can therefore occur in a ferrimagnet too. Identifying a real magnetic structure needs the full crystal basis structure factor, multiple reflections, and the allowed moment orientations, rather than a single extra peak.
Magnetic form factor
Words: 22
Magnetic neutron diffraction OurBigBook.com
The scattering-vector dependence of magnetic scattering from the spatial distribution of a magnetic moment, commonly suppressing magnetic intensity at large momentum transfer.
Manganese monoxide neutron diffraction experiment
Words: 368
Magnetic neutron diffraction OurBigBook.com
In 1949, Clifford Shull and J. Samuel Smart compared powdered manganese(II) oxide at room temperature and 80K. Powder preparation supplies many crystal orientations. Their Fig. 1 records scattered-neutron intensity versus counter angle. Nuclear reflections remained, while the cold pattern gained strong reflections forbidden by the chemical unit cell. They indexed these with a magnetic unit cell having twice the chemical cell edge. The warm pattern already contained diffuse magnetic scattering: loss of sharp magnetic peaks does not mean loss of individual magnetic moments.[ref]
The source was Oak Ridge's graphite-moderated reactor. In Early Development of Neutron Scattering (1994), Clifford Shull describes how the early two-axis instruments used a monochromating crystal to select the incident-neutron wavelength; a shielded neutron counter rotated around the specimen to record angular intensity. This specifies the source–monochromator–sample–counter path, without identifying which instrument revision produced the MnO trace.[ref]
The control was the same compound above and below magnetic ordering, with retained nuclear peaks identifying the underlying chemical periodicity. The original paper labels an aluminium impurity peak and defers a complete magnetic-structure account. It supplies neither a chemical synthesis recipe nor detailed cold-stage construction. The inference is periodic magnetic order, rather than a claim that every possible structural change was excluded at arbitrary resolution.[ref]
The connection to the measured angle is the elastic Bragg scattering condition. If the incident and outgoing wave vectors have equal magnitude 2π/λ and make an angle 2θ, their difference has magnitude
∣Q∣=λ4π​sinθ.
(118)
A longer real-space period supplies additional, smaller reciprocal lattice spacings, which can put magnetic reflections at new counter angles. In the one-dimensional toy model above, doubling the period changes the allowed spacing from 2π/a to π/a. The actual MnO indexing is three-dimensional; the toy row does not assert its reflection positions or relative peak strengths.
Louis Néel supplied the ordering theory; the 1949 diffraction work was a later experimental test. His 1970 Nobel Prize in Physics recognized antiferromagnetism and ferrimagnetism. Clifford Shull's neutron-diffraction award followed in 1994.[ref]

Exchange interaction

Words: 776 Articles: 10
Magnetism OurBigBook.com
The exchange interaction is an effective interaction between spins originating in the quantum mechanics of electrons. Its sign convention must accompany any formula. For the illustrative classical fixed-length spin pair used here, write
E=JS1​⋅S2​=JS2cosθ.
(119)
With this plus-sign convention, J>0 favors antiparallel spins: E(π)=−JS2, compared with E(0)=+JS2. The energy difference is 2JS2. If instead the Hamiltonian is written with an overall minus sign, the same physical preference has a negative coupling. This prevents a sign convention in the Ising model from being mistaken for a disagreement about the ordering.

Indirect exchange

Words: 111 Articles: 1
Exchange interaction OurBigBook.com
Magnetic moments can interact through intermediate orbitals or itinerant carriers rather than direct overlap alone. Superexchange uses virtual charge transfer, the RKKY interaction uses conduction-electron spin response, and double exchange gains carrier kinetic energy through spin-dependent hopping. More than one mechanism can operate in the same solid, with different signs and ranges.
RKKY interaction
Words: 64
Indirect exchange OurBigBook.com
A local moment induces conduction-electron spin polarization, which mediates a second-order coupling to another moment. The static electronic spin susceptibility fixes the spatial interaction. For a three-dimensional spherical Fermi surface its leading large-distance form oscillates as cos(2kF​R)/R3, up to the overall sign convention and prefactor. The sign alternates with separation. Other band structures and dimensions change this form. [ref]

Exponential orbital-tail estimate of exchange (∣t(d)∣∼P(d)e−κd,J∼4∣t∣2/U)

Words: 63
Exchange interaction OurBigBook.com
For localized orbitals with an exponential tail e−κr, overlap-mediated hopping over separation d inherits an exponentially small factor e−κd, multiplied by geometry-dependent polynomial factors. A kinetic-exchange scale then falls approximately as e−2κd. Comparisons must use actual nearest-neighbour distances, not interchange lattice constants between different crystal structures. The estimate is not a replacement for a screened solid-state orbital calculation.

Conduction-electron-mediated exchange

Words: 92
Exchange interaction OurBigBook.com
A localized magnetic moment can polarize a metal's conduction electrons, whose response changes the energy of a second moment. This indirect exchange interaction can be long ranged and oscillate in sign with separation because of the Fermi surface. In the three-dimensional isotropic free-electron asymptotic limit its range dependence is proportional to cos(2kF​r)/r3, with coupling-dependent prefactor and sign convention. The original calculation for nuclear moments used their contact hyperfine interaction with conduction electrons; it was motivated by nuclear magnetic resonance line widths in metallic silver.[ref]

Double-exchange mechanism

Words: 81
Exchange interaction OurBigBook.com
Double exchange couples localized magnetic moments through actual carrier hopping between sites of different valence. Strong local Hund's coupling makes hopping energetically easier when neighboring core spins align, lowering the carrier kinetic energy. In the classical strong-coupling limit, a common effective hopping is teff​=tcos(θ/2) for relative spin angle θ; aligned cores maximize its magnitude. Unlike insulating superexchange, this mechanism directly connects carrier motion and magnetic alignment.[ref]

Coulomb exchange splitting of two orbitals (E±​=ϵa​+ϵb​+J±K)

Words: 105
Exchange interaction OurBigBook.com
Let a,b be distinct orthonormal spatial orbitals occupied by two identical spin one-half particles, with a weak repulsive Coulomb interaction. The symmetric and antisymmetric spatial combinations have first-order energy shifts J+K and J−K, where J is the direct Coulomb integral and
K=g∫d3rd3r′∣r−r′∣a∗(r)b(r)b∗(r′)a(r′)​,g>0.
(120)
The Coulomb kernel has positive Fourier transform 4π/∣k∣2, so K≥0. Fermionic exchange symmetry pairs the symmetric spatial function with the spin-one-half singlet state and the antisymmetric one with the spin-one-half triplet state. For these fixed orbitals the triplet lies lower by 2K when K>0. This does not compare arbitrary singlets and triplets with different orbital occupations; for negligible orbital overlap the splitting can vanish.

Superexchange

Words: 133 Articles: 1
Exchange interaction OurBigBook.com
Superexchange couples localized moments through virtual hopping via intermediate, often nonmagnetic, ligand orbitals. Half-filled orbitals sharing an effective hopping amplitude t give an antiferromagnetic scale J≃4∣t∣2/U in the repulsive one-band limit. Ligand geometry, orbital occupation and exchange within intermediate states can change the balance and allow ferromagnetic coupling. Real charge motion can remain gapped while these virtual processes couple an insulating magnet's spins.
Three-site charge-transfer superexchange (J∼4tpd4​/(Δ2Ud​))
Words: 71
Superexchange OurBigBook.com
In a minimal hole description of a metal–ligand–metal path, two holes initially occupy separate metal orbitals and the ligand has no hole. Creating a virtual ligand hole costs a charge-transfer energy Δ. Two hops generate an effective metal–metal hopping of order tpd2​/Δ; two more hops through metal double occupancy generate the antiferromagnetic scale in the title. Ligand double occupancy adds a channel with denominator 2Δ+Up​. Orbital geometry and intra-atomic exchange determine when the antiferromagnetic channel dominates.

Direct exchange

Words: 106 Articles: 1
Exchange interaction OurBigBook.com
Direct exchange comes from Coulomb matrix elements between overlapping localized electronic orbitals together with the antisymmetry required by the Pauli exclusion principle. It produces a spin-dependent energy without being a classical dipole interaction. Its competition with kinetic processes and orbital occupation helps determine whether neighbouring moments prefer parallel or antiparallel alignment.
Direct Coulomb exchange versus kinetic exchange
Words: 59
Direct exchange OurBigBook.com
A direct intersite Coulomb exchange integral acts without an intermediate doubly occupied state. In a repulsive one-band Hubbard model, by contrast, virtual hopping into a doubly occupied state lowers the singlet energy by 4t2/U relative to the triplet. The latter is antiferromagnetic kinetic exchange, even when hopping is directly between neighbouring magnetic orbitals. Ligand-mediated superexchange introduces an intermediate ligand orbital as well.

Antiferromagnetism

Words: 283 Articles: 5
Magnetism OurBigBook.com
Antiferromagnetism is ordered compensation of magnetic moments. In the collinear two-sublattice model, MA​=−MB​=0: net magnetization vanishes but staggered magnetization remains. Louis Néel developed this possibility.[ref]
For an original local energy check, perturb the antiparallel pair in exchange interaction by writing θ=π−δ. Then
E=−JS2cosδ=−JS2+21​JS2δ2+O(δ4).
(121)
For J>0, a small relative rotation costs positive energy. This verifies a pair's preference; it does not prove a bulk ordering temperature. A whole crystal must satisfy many bonds simultaneously, and thermal fluctuations and quantum effects matter. The Heisenberg antiferromagnet and antiferromagnetic Ising model specify different assumptions about those collective degrees of freedom.
Why is the distinction useful? A measurement of zero magnetization cannot decide between an ordered alternating arrangement, a disordered ensemble, and oppositely magnetized magnetic domains. A spatial probe such as magnetic neutron diffraction tests the pattern directly. The manganese monoxide neutron diffraction experiment is a particularly clear example: the order adds a new periodic scattering signal even though the net magnetic moment cancels.

Two or more ferromagnetic layers coupled to favour antiparallel alignment, often through a thin spacer. Compensating their magnetic moments reduces net stray fields while retaining a useful reference magnetization in spintronic structures.

Néel temperature (TN​)

Words: 70
Antiferromagnetism OurBigBook.com
The Néel temperature marks loss of long-range antiferromagnetism. A Curie temperature concerns ferromagnetism or ferrimagnetism; magnetic compensation temperature instead denotes cancellation within an ordered ferrimagnet.[ref]
In the simple collinear description, compare ∣L∣ across TN​, rather than expecting ∣M∣ to switch from nonzero to zero. Zero-field magnetization may be zero on both sides. A nonzero magnetic susceptibility is also compatible with antiferromagnetism: an applied magnetic field can disturb the cancellation. The uniform response of a two-sublattice Ising antiferromagnet provides a model calculation.

Ferrimagnetism

Words: 303 Articles: 1
Magnetism OurBigBook.com
Ferrimagnetism has opposing, generally unequal ordered magnetic sublattices, with net magnetization ∣MA​−MB​∣ in a collinear model. Louis Néel used it to explain magnetic oxides.[ref]
The counting example in magnetic sublattice gives 3(2m0​)−3(m0​)=3m0​. Unequal populations also suffice: four sites carrying +m0​ and two carrying −m0​ give 2m0​, even with identical individual magnitudes. Thus one must compare total sublattice contributions per common volume, rather than merely asking whether two atomic species carry different magnetic moments.
Both ferromagnetism and ferrimagnetism can produce a macroscopic magnet. Their internal organization differs: the latter retains opposing contributions. This makes ferrimagnetism a useful bridge between net magnetization and microscopic magnetic order: reducing one opposing contribution can increase the net sum, even though the total sum of moment magnitudes decreases.

Magnetic compensation temperature (Tcomp​)

Words: 187
Ferrimagnetism OurBigBook.com
At a magnetic compensation temperature, MA​=MB​=0: an ordered ferrimagnet has zero net magnetization. Such cancellation need not occur in every material.[ref]
For an original stipulated example, let t=T/TC​, with 0≤t≤1, and prescribe sublattice magnitudes per common volume by
MA​(t)=M0​(1−t),MB​(t)=23​M0​(1−t)2,M0​>0.
(122)
Take A along +z and B along −z, retaining a fixed sublattice orientation convention. These are toy functions, not measured curves or a self-consistent mean-field approximation. Their difference factors exactly:
Mz​(t)=MA​−MB​=2M0​​(1−t)(3t−1).
(123)
At t=0, Mz​=−M0​/2. At t=1/3, both magnitudes equal 2M0​/3 and Mz​=0: this is compensation with finite order. At t=1/2, Mz​=M0​/8>0. At t=1, both magnitudes vanish: that endpoint represents the stipulated Curie temperature, not another compensation point. For t>1 stipulate both ordered magnitudes zero; do not extrapolate the polynomials into negative sublattice magnitudes.
The sign change refers to the net component relative to the fixed A direction. A freely reorienting specimen in an applied magnetic field need not display this signed branch directly. The example isolates the cancellation mechanism; it predicts neither a material's transition temperature nor its response to magnetic domains or an applied magnetic field.
